primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic kidney disease (advanced DKD) with stage 4 CKD

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after any dose change
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression; control hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine & potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: Amlodipine 5 mg orally once daily (increase to 10 mg if needed)
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually or when blood pressure target not met
medications.purpose: Additional blood pressure control if target <130/80 mmHg not achieved with ACE‑I alone
medications.nice_justification: NG203 non‑pharmacological BP target <130/80 mmHg for ACR ≥70 mg/mmol; CCB safe in advanced CKD

medications.duration: Until corrected calcium and phosphate are within target range — review every 4 weeks
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends active vitamin D analogues for CKD‑MBD after confirming calcium/phosphate status

medications.dose: Epoetin alfa 50 IU/kg subcutaneously weekly (dose adjusted to maintain Hb 10–11 g/dL)
medications.duration: Until hemoglobin 10–11 g/dL is achieved — review monthly
medications.purpose: Treat anemia of chronic kidney disease
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises ESA therapy for CKD‑related anemia after iron repletion and Hb <10 g/dL

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and increase risk of AKI; eGFR 10.9 mL/min/1.73 m²
eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Insulin or other glucose‑lowering agents appropriate for advanced CKD

contraindications.reason: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy
contraindications.alternative: Use prophylactic hydration and low‑osmolar contrast if imaging unavoidable

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium, sodium, bicarbonate, calcium, phosphate, PTH, and liver function tests are required before initiating Ramipril, Calcitriol, and Atorvastatin.
Blood pressure reading not provided; amlodipine is planned only if target <130/80 mmHg is not achieved with ACE‑I alone.
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) are needed before starting ESA; ESA will be initiated only after iron repletion.
Allergy status to ACE‑I, statin, vitamin D analogue, and ESA is unknown – verify before prescribing.
Patient is not on any OTC or herbal medications; confirm absence of NSAID use at each visit.
treatment_summary: Start Ramipril 1.25 mg daily and Atorvastatin 20 mg daily as first‑line therapy for CKD progression and cardiovascular risk. Add Amlodipine 5 mg daily if blood pressure remains above target. Initiate Calcitriol 0.25 µg daily for CKD‑MBD after confirming calcium/phosphate status, and consider Epoetin alfa weekly for anemia once iron stores are optimized. Avoid NSAIDs, metformin, dual ACE‑I/ARB, lithium, and unprotected IV contrast. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, lipids, calcium/phosphate, and hemoglobin according to NG203 recommendations.
